remaining_tasks.name: Handle Spotify songs not on YouTube gracefully

blockers.description: SSL CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED for music.youtube.com. spotDL and ytmusicapi both fail. Only yt-dlp (--no-check-certificate) and requests to open.spotify.com work.
blockers.workaround: Use ONLY yt-dlp ytsearch: for YouTube. Do NOT add any library making direct HTTPS to music.youtube.com.

blockers.description: Some Spotify songs do not exist on YouTube at all (e.g. the tested song 'Volver a Nacer' by Vicco — only Chayanne has a song with this title on YouTube). No ytsearch query can return a non-existent video.
blockers.workaround: Show user an error/warning when no match found instead of downloading wrong song. Consider letting user paste a direct YouTube URL as override.

human_actions_pending.action: Decide UX for songs not found on YouTube: show error row, skip, or let user provide YouTube URL
human_actions_pending.context: Current fallback downloads wrong song silently — bad UX for public launch

decisions.decision: Do NOT use ytmusicapi or spotDL
_find_best_yt_match: quoted title search + title substring match
decisions.rationale: More precise than unquoted, but cannot find songs absent from YouTube

decisions.decision: No artist/song names in code or commits

next_action: Fix: when _find_best_yt_match returns None AND ytsearch also fails to find the right song, show the row as FAILED with a message like 'Song not found on YouTube — paste a direct YouTube URL'. This prevents silently downloading wrong content.
context_notes: Root cause found: some Spotify songs are simply not on YouTube. No matching algorithm can fix this. The correct UX is to surface the failure clearly and let the user provide a direct YouTube URL as a fallback. The _find_best_yt_match function itself is working correctly — it's the source data that's missing.
